definitions.explanation: Indicates something lasting indefinitely without change or reversal. More factual and formal than {永遠|えいえん}に, often used for official, legal, or scientific permanence.

examples.japanese: この{記録|きろく}は{永久|えいきゅう}に{保存|ほぞん}される。
examples.english: This record will be preserved permanently.

examples.japanese: {永久|えいきゅう}に{使|つか}える{保証|ほしょう}はない。
examples.english: There is no guarantee it will last forever.

examples.japanese: あの{種|しゅ}は{絶滅|ぜつめつ}して、{永久|えいきゅう}に{地球|ちきゅう}から{姿|すがた}を{消|け}した。
examples.english: That species went extinct and disappeared from the Earth for good.

examples.japanese: {資源|しげん}が{永久|えいきゅう}に{続|つづ}くわけではない。

notes:
Adverbial form of {永久|えいきゅう} (permanence; eternity) + に. Compared to {永遠|えいえん}に, this word is more objective, factual, and formal. It is preferred in scientific, legal, and official contexts where genuine permanence is at stake.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {永久|えいきゅう}に{保存|ほぞん}する: to preserve permanently
- {永久|えいきゅう}に{失|うしな}われる: to be permanently lost
- {永久|えいきゅう}に{続|つづ}く: to continue perpetually
- {永久|えいきゅう}に{凍結|とうけつ}する: to freeze permanently

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {永遠|えいえん}に: forever; eternally — more emotional and literary, used for feelings, memories, and hyperbole
- {恒久的|こうきゅうてき}に: permanently — formal/official synonym, used in policy and institutional contexts
- {半永久的|はんえいきゅうてき}に: semi-permanently — indicates very long but not truly infinite duration
